title: Console shell surfaces are self-configured from the applied capability sidecar at deploy time, not from client-side inference
asA: admin operator opening the console the same way in every deploy environment
iWant: the shell to read the applied capability set from a deterministic sidecar file, not to infer from a client-side probe
soThat: a preview build renders the same nav a production build renders on the same commit

acceptanceCriteria.description: The console shell reads rcf/blueprints/application-admin-console.applied.json (written by apply at build time) as a build asset served under a stable path (e.g. /admin/caps.json); the shell never runs a runtime probe against manifest.blueprints[] over the network. The sidecar payload shape is owned by TAC-2201.interfaces.capabilitiesSidecar.

When manifest.blueprints[] carries a library-qualified source that cannot be read locally (a library-qualified source unavailable at read time), the entry is skipped in the union; the sidecar (shape owned by TAC-2201.interfaces.capabilitiesSidecar) records the skipped entry and the shell navigation gates as though that source had contributed no capabilities (no surface renders that would have required a capability from the missing source).
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project whose manifest.blueprints[] names a library-qualified source unavailable locally
acceptanceCriteria.when: apply runs and the sidecar is written
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sidecar entry names the skipped source id per TAC-2201.interfaces.capabilitiesSidecar and the shell navigation renders only surfaces whose gating capabilities were provided by successfully read sources
